📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France.

Industry observers note that there may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling.

Sources indicate that which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal’s under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer. He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records.

In scoring his first under-21s goal, in the penultimate minute of regular time, Dowman eclipsed Jude Bellingham to become the team’s youngest scorer at 16 years and 320 days, three days after surpassing the Real Madrid midfielder’s record as the under-21s’ youngest player. Bellingham was almost four months older than Dowman when he scored his first goal for the age group, in September 2020. Bellingham made only four appearances for the under-21s, a result of being fast-tracked into the senior team, and Dowman could emulate him again, though he is expected to feature in next summer’s Under-21 European Championship in Albania and Serbia.

In a recent development, the common view from coaches and teammates, and something stressed by Lee Carsley, the under-21s head coach, is that it is easy to forget Dowman is a month shy of his 17th birthday. Against France, it was also extremely easy to overlook that this was Dowman’s first start for the under-21s, after a substitute appearance against Portugal last Friday. His first action set the tone on Monday, using his body to box off the ball then jinking up the right flank, zipping it through the legs of Dayann Methalie before skating forward and sending the Sunderland left-back juddering on to his backside.

Dowman exhibited plenty of neat touches, a couple of effortless first-time passes, but those who have watched him develop say his work rate and willingness to do the other side of the game is one of his biggest strengths. “We look at Max and see how good he is on the ball, how attacking he is, but I thought he was outstanding off the ball,” Carsley said, presumably thinking of the moment Dowman scampered deep into his own half to intercept a stray France pass. He was not finished after scoring either. At one point he had five blue shirts haring after him as he stormed into the France half and, seconds later, his quick feet lured opposition captain, Nathan Zézé, into a foul on the edge of the box.

According to recent reports, dowman is among the next wave of players pushing to step up to Thomas Tuchel’s squad, perhaps at its forefront. It is a well-trodden path and the current crop need not look too far for inspiration. Elliot Anderson and Jarell Quansah, both of whom started England’s triumph at the last under-21 Euros in Bratislava, began Sunday’s memorable victory for the seniors in Madrid. Jobe Bellingham and Josh King are the latest players to make the transition into Tuchel’s squad and more will follow.

In a recent development, jack Hinshelwood and Trey Nyoni, of Brighton and Liverpool respectively, impressed at the base of midfield and the 19-year-old Mikey Moore, another to score on his first start for the under-21s, shone down the left flank, opening the scoring. The Everton midfielder Harrison Armstrong entered as a substitute and supplied Dowman’s winner, and Armstrong’s clubmate Tyrique George also demonstrated promise after replacing Moore. Archie Gray captained the under-21s against Portugal but did not feature on Monday, with Carsley revealing he has spoken to the Tottenham midfielder about Scotland wanting him to switch allegiance. “I just said to him: ‘Keep me in the picture, if it’s something that you were thinking of,’” Carsley said. “I think Archie is very connected to our pathway.”.

It has been revealed that england’s budding talent is not confined to the under-21s. Carsley took a closer look at Brian Madjo, the imposing 17-year-old striker who scored on his Aston Villa debut in the Super Cup in August, the Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven and the West Brom forward Jimmy-Jay Morgan, who signed from Chelsea in the summer, before his squad departed for Bristol last week, the trio joining the under-21s for four days of training at St George’s Park.

According to recent reports, dowman, after two under-21 appearances comprising a total of a little more than 120 minutes, is putting the squeeze on. “Max is doing something special for his age and he is pushing people a lot older than him,” said Moore, who is on loan from Tottenham at Köln and hopes to face his idol Harry Kane and Bayern Munich on Friday. “He’s a top kid. You kind of forget how old he is. My little brother is 17 and he [Dowman] feels older to me than my little brother … He has been top and everywhere he goes, he just takes that next step.”.

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

It’s Time to Run an Audit of All the Cloud Storage Links You’ve Shared

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cloud storage certainly has a lot going for it.
  • Then there's file sharing: Not too many years ago, swapping large amounts of data with other people meant dragging and dropping and running around with USB drives (and perhaps even mailing them).
  • However, this comes with security risks attached.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cloud storage certainly has a lot going for it. For a start, if you drop your laptop into the sink, it's likely that a lot of your important work will be backed up somewhere in the cloud, as long as you’re using services such as Google Drive, OneDrive, and iCloud.

Then there's file sharing: Not too many years ago, swapping large amounts of data with other people meant dragging and dropping and running around with USB drives (and perhaps even mailing them). Now, via a couple of clicks and a link, you can share just about anything with just about anyone, anywhere in the world.

However, this comes with security risks attached. You don't want those links making their way to anyone they weren't intended for; otherwise, they’ve got access to your files and folders. They could potentially see what’s in them and maybe even make changes or delete files, depending on the permissions you’ve set.

According to recent reports, it’s worth emphasizing that sharing files through these cloud storage services isn't inherently insecure—these shared links are actually very well protected by default. However, the longer they stick around, the bigger the risk gets. Your links could get mistakenly forwarded in an email, or one of your contacts could have their email account hacked.

According to recent reports, with that in mind, it’s prudent to run a regular audit on the cloud-sharing links you’ve got active. It shouldn’t take long: The apps involved usually make this pretty straightforward. Once you’ve closed a link down, no one else can get to it.

If you head to the Microsoft OneDrive portal on the web, you’ll see a Shared link in the navigation pane on the left: Click this, then select By you up at the top of the file list to see everything you’ve shared with other people. Use the Modified header if you want to sort the files and folders by the oldest or most recent.

Click the three dots next to any file or folder, then Manage access to control who can get to it. If you've shared the file with specific people, you can remove some or all of them; if the file or folder is shared more widely with just a link, clicking the trash can gets rid of it. You can also open up Office files to manage access there.

It’s worth knowing that when you opt to share a file in OneDrive on the web (via the three dots and Share), if you click the cog icon on the Share panel, you can set an expiration date for the sharing—which saves you the trouble of having to tidy it up afterward.

In a recent development, if iCloud Drive is your cloud storage service of choice, once you’ve got the main interface up on the web, you can click Shared on the navigation pane on the left to go straight to the files and folders you’re sharing with other people. There’s no easy way to sort them, but you can use the search box up in the top right corner.

It has been revealed that click the three dots next to a file or folder, then Managed Shared File to make changes. The next screen lets you block access for specific contacts and change permissions (from editing to just viewing, for example). If you want to cancel the sharing altogether, click Stop sharing.

Unlike OneDrive, iCloud doesn’t give you any way of putting expiration periods on shared links, so you have to clear them up manually.

Dropbox is one of the more aggressive services when it comes to tidying up shared links, and if you use one of the Dropbox apps you might see reminders to review the files and folders you’ve shared with others. From Dropbox on the web, click Shared in the left-hand navigation pane to see files and folders you’re right now sharing.

According to recent reports, you can get quite a detailed breakdown here, including by Files or by Folders. Click the three dots next to any entry, then Share, to see the current sharing options: You can remove access for contacts one by one, or click the cog icon (top left) to find the Unshare button that ends all sharing completely.

According to recent reports, dropbox does have link expiration features built in: If you open the share settings whenever you’re sharing a file or folder, you’ll see Link expiry as one of the options. It’s an easy way to keep things tidy, provided the people you’re sharing the file or folder with get around to viewing it in time.

Sources indicate that google Drive isn't quite as on top of shared links as other cloud storage services. If you open up the web portal, there’s no easy-to-access list of everything you've shared. The closest thing to it is clicking the People filter and then choosing contacts to see files and folders you've shared with them specifically. If you pick Anyone with the link from the drop-down list, you’ll see everything shared with a simple link.

To change the sharing settings for a file or folder, click on the three dots, then Share. Click the cog icon on the panel that pops up, then you can remove contacts as needed and turn the visible link off.

In a recent development, as with iCloud, there’s no link expiration feature you can rely on here, so shared files and folders can’t be set to become unshared after a certain time has elapsed. It’s a shame Google doesn’t make it as easy as it could be.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gianni Infantino has been president of Fifa since 2016 and is standing for re-election for a third time.

Uefa has finally identified a candidate to take on Gianni Infantino in next year's Fifa presidential election.

Less than 48 hours before Wednesday night's deadline, European football's governing body revealed that French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe Diallo had received the unanimous support of its executive committee.

A late and surprise choice, Diallo remarked, "I think I have the experience, the convictions and the values which offer a credible alternative.".

But he is not the Frenchman some believe Uefa really wanted, as it tries to remove Infantino in the wake of his failed proposal to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Recent findings suggest that senior figures in European football had hoped to persuade Arsene Wenger - Fifa's head of global development - to stand against his own boss. Some felt that only he had the credibility and unifying potential to be able to pose a serious threat to Infantino's plans for a fourth term.

But after the former Arsenal manager chose not to proceed, Uefa had no choice but to seek an alternative.

According to recent reports, so just how credible a challenger is Diallo? Does Infantino's position appear unassailable? And how could he still be stopped from winning another term?

Wenger decides not to challenge Fifa chief Infantino.

Politicians, private jets and power - the life of a Fifa president.

Industry observers note that an administrator who has worked in French football since 1992 and became FFF president in 2023, Diallo is not a household name. But he has already shown he is prepared to stand up to Infantino.

In September, Diallo claimed he had "seriously damaged the image and unity of football", and stated "trust has been broken" over the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) sell-off plot.

According to Uefa vice-president Laura McAllister, Diallo is a "candidate who can instigate real, meaningful and lasting reform" within the governing body.

"We've always made it very clear that our objectives and motivations are driving culture change. That means wide-ranging, systemic reform of football governance rather than simply the replacement of an individual leader," McAllister told BBC Sport.

"I've known Philippe since we were both elected to Uefa's executive committee, and he's an intelligent, honest, sharp-minded football person with an impressive experience of governance in one of the world's football power-houses. Most importantly, he is a person of integrity... Philippe is a fantastic advocate for the change agenda that football needs, and I know his campaign will reflect that.".

Infantino remains the favourite to win a majority of the 211 votes, and is thought to have the support of most of Africa (54 members), Asia (47) and South America (10).

However, Uefa hopes that Diallo - whose father was a Senegalese boxing champion who represented France in the 1960 Olympics - could enjoy support in parts of Africa and beyond. He claims he already has the backing of countries beyond Europe.

Laura McAllister is a former captain of the Wales women's football team.

In a recent development, while most of Europe's national associations are expected to vote for Diallo, it is clear that he was not Uefa's first choice. "I wasn't initially a candidate, but the insistence of my European colleagues led me to accept the offer", he admitted.

Uefa only approached Diallo about standing in the past week, and senior officials at some European national associations have also told BBC Sport they are frustrated with the failure to find a higher-profile candidate sooner.

Speaking anonymously, one mentioned they only learned about Diallo's potential candidacy on Sunday, and that while they were supportive of him, "it would have been helpful if we'd had someone much earlier" and "a lot of eggs were put in the Wenger basket.".

They also made the point that Diallo was yet to publish a manifesto, and questioned whether he could really win.

Sources indicate that another expressed similar sentiments, saying Diallo was a good man, but "not seen as a heavyweight". They claimed that Uefa had "lost the momentum. The process hasn't been great. I really hope they've got a rabbit to pull out of the hat.".

Industry observers note that mcAllister is optimistic: "I have no doubt whatsoever that we will collectively mount a powerful campaign with the objective of winning the election next March". she said.

"The really critical period comes next, once candidate nominations close and eligibility checks are complete.".

Despite high-profile critics like Germany manager Jurgen Klopp - who this week said "the opinion is unanimous that a change would make sense" - Infantino does appear to be in a position of strength.

As recently as August it all seemed very different when the heads of three confederations - Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf, which runs the game in North and Central America - signed a letter accusing the Fifa president of breaking trust "through deception".

In a recent development, amid an increasingly acrimonious civil war, Infantino seemed vulnerable. But the revolt against him then suffered some setbacks.

Uefa called off a threatened boycott of Fifa competitions, and then potential rivals such as Concacaf chief Victor Montagliani decided not to stand. Aleksander Ceferin chose to stand for a fourth term as Uefa president rather than challenge Infantino directly.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, Infantino's position as the incumbent enabled him to embark on what has appeared to be a world tour, shoring up support. His chances of re-election received another major boost when he proposed to increase the amount of money handed out by Fifa for football development across the world by Â£2.6 billion.

Sheikh Salman, the head of the Asian Football Confederation, then performed a U-turn, endorsing Infantino, who soon after told the BBC he had the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football.

"I'm a professor of politics so I never assume that there's a runaway favourite to win any election", insists McAllister.

"There are plenty of twists and turns to come in this story between now and the election at Fifa's Congress next year.

"This is about structural change and a commitment to modernising the way in which football is governed so it benefits all who play and watch...that imperative will remain and we will hold the new president accountable for much-needed change.".

"The current weaknesses of global football governance have been brutally exposed of late. This has helped coalesce and unite opposition to Gianni Infantino, but also to articulate the widely-held demands that things must change.".

So with just four months until the presidential election, where could Infantino still run into difficulties?

It has been revealed that litigation is arguably the most obvious. As part of its wider proposal to remove Infantino, Uefa has filed court documents in the US, which includes a potential criminal complaint against him in Switzerland for alleged financial mismanagement.

It has been revealed that the legal action has not yet appeared to trouble him. But some senior figures in the European game remain hopeful it could still force Fifa to hand over evidence related to FFE that could prove damaging to Infantino's re-election prospects.

Sources indicate that there is pressure from elsewhere in football. Fifa has already agreed to make "key documents" relating to the FFE strategy available to members of its council. Infantino's critics believe this disclosure may reveal details that could increase the pressure on him before the election. Last month, the Norwegian Football Federation also submitted a three-part ethics complaint to Fifa regarding the awarding of a Peace Prize to US President Donald Trump, the Folarin Balogun case at the World Cup, and the FFE plot.

It has been revealed that the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections means scrutiny from beyond the sport too. Earlier this year, Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee launched an inquiry into Infantino's ties with Trump. In September, a spokeswoman mentioned FIfa's co-operation with the investigation had been "woefully inadequate." But armed with extra powers, they could now force him to hand over relevant documents or give evidence.

Recent months have also seen a series of potentially damaging stories emerge in the media about various aspects of Infantino's leadership. So far they seem to have done little harm to his re-election chances, with Fifa claiming "it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine [him]". But the scrutiny is likely to continue.

Could Infantino even be ruled ineligible to stand? According to Portuguese lawyer Miguel Maduro - a former head of Fifa's governance committee - Infantino should not be allowed to be a candidate in the election as Fifa rules limit presidents to three terms. In 2022, Fifa's Council agreed that his first period in office - between 2016 and 2019 - should not count as he was effectively completing the remainder of Blatter's term after his resignation. But as Maduro has said, a national association or confederation would need to challenge this decision at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

According to recent reports, japan Football Association honorary president, Kozo Tashima, has revealed his intention to stand, along with former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega. But with uncertainty over how much support either man will have, it seems Diallo is the challenger most likely to test the strength of Infantino's supporter base. There is a danger that the vote against Infantino is split.

It has not gone unnoticed at Fifa that as recently as March, Diallo was quoted congratulating Infantino when the Fifa president visited Paris, external to highlight a mini-pitch programme and the need for more football infrastructure globally.

Industry observers note that A lot has changed since then, however. And now the Frenchman has been tasked with finding a way of unseating Infantino, and becoming just the 10th Fifa president in its history.

#13007. After 40 years, CERN finds evidence of a one-in-10-billion particle decay

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1075 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

After 40 years, CERN finds evidence of a one-in-10-billion particle decay

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1075 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After more than 40 years of searching, physicists at CERN have reached a major milestone in their hunt for one of the rarest known particle decays.
  • Industry observers note that the finding, revealed during a seminar at CERN, marks the first time a single experiment has produced sufficient evidence for this extraordinarily rare event.
  • Sources indicate that at the center of the discovery is a particle called Bd, which contains a beauty quark and a down antiquark.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After more than 40 years of searching, physicists at CERN have reached a major milestone in their hunt for one of the rarest known particle decays. Researchers working with the LHCb experiment have detected evidence of a process expected to occur only once in approximately 10 billion beauty particle decays.

Industry observers note that the finding, revealed during a seminar at CERN, marks the first time a single experiment has produced sufficient evidence for this extraordinarily rare event. Beyond its rarity, the decay is particularly valuable because it could help scientists investigate particles that are too massive to be created directly in the Large Hadron Collider.

Sources indicate that at the center of the discovery is a particle called Bd, which contains a beauty quark and a down antiquark. Scientists found evidence that this particle can decay into a pair of muons (μ+μ-). Muons are similar to electrons but have greater mass. The results agree with predictions from the Standard Model, the leading theory describing fundamental particles and their interactions, and help narrow the possibilities for new particles beyond it.

Why Rare Particle Decays Could Reveal Latest Physics.

It has been revealed that one reason physicists are so interested in these unusual decays is that quantum effects allow other particles to influence how they occur. Even particles too heavy to be produced in the Large Hadron Collider can potentially leave subtle traces in the rates of these processes.

Recent findings suggest that by measuring extremely rare decays with high precision, researchers can look for differences between experimental results and theoretical predictions. Such discrepancies could provide indirect evidence of previously unknown particles. Generally, the rarer a decay is, the more sensitive it can be to these hidden influences.

Sources indicate that the decay known as Bd → μ+μ-belongs to a special category that physicists have long considered 'golden channels' for investigating physics beyond the Standard Model. During this process, a beauty quark and an antiquark with the opposite electric charge annihilate each other. Their energy is transformed into a muon and its antiparticle.

Scientists have previously observed a related process involving a different beauty particle, called Bs. In 2015, a joint analysis by the LHCb and CMS collaborations reported the first confirmed observation of Bs → μ+μ-, along with initial evidence for the much rarer Bd decay.

It has been revealed that however, subsequent analyses incorporating data collected through 2018 could not confirm the earlier evidence for Bd → μ+μ-. The difference in rarity is substantial. The Bs decay occurs approximately three times per billion beauty particle decays, while the Bd process is predicted to happen about 30 times less frequently.

Upgraded CERN Detector Makes the Breakthrough Possible.

A significant improvement to the LHCb experiment helped researchers overcome the enormous difficulty of detecting such a rare event.

It has been revealed that following a major upgrade, the experiment began collecting data in 2024 at five times the rate achieved between 2010 and 2018. The upgraded detector also became better at identifying different kinds of particles, giving researchers a clearer picture of the activity produced during collisions.

Sources indicate that the team combined these improvements with machine learning techniques to distinguish the exceptionally rare signals from the vast number of other particle processes. Without these advances, the events scientists wanted to study would have been overwhelmed by the background.

"Physicists have been chasing this decay for more than forty years," mentioned Marco Santimaria, who co-led the international analysis team of 19 scientists. "Extreme precision is required to pick the muons out of the overwhelming background.".

Four Decades of Searching Finally Produce Strong Evidence.

In particle physics, scientists use a statistical measure called standard deviations to evaluate how likely an apparent signal is to result from random fluctuations rather than a genuine physical process.

A result must reach three standard deviations to qualify as evidence of a new phenomenon. At that level, the probability of random fluctuations producing a signal at least as statistically extreme is approximately 0.3%.

Using data collected during 2024 and 2025, the LHCb researchers identified evidence of Bd → μ+μ- at a significance of 3.0 standard deviations. When they combined those measurements with earlier data gathered between 2011 and 2018, the statistical significance increased to 3.2 standard deviations, exceeding the widely accepted threshold for evidence.

The same investigation also produced the most precise measurements ever obtained for the related Bs → μ+μ-decay, providing additional information about these exceptionally uncommon processes.

Although the new findings represent a major achievement, physicists have not yet reached the threshold required to declare a confirmed observation. That milestone requires a significance of five standard deviations.

If future measurements achieve that level of certainty, Bd → μ+μ-would become the rarest beauty particle decay ever observed.

Future Large Hadron Collider Upgrades Could Uncover Hidden Particles.

Researchers expect upcoming improvements to the Large Hadron Collider to make these measurements even more powerful.

Recent findings suggest that the High Luminosity LHC, also known as the HiLumi LHC, is scheduled to begin operating in 2030. Another major upgrade to the LHCb experiment is planned for the middle of the following decade. Together, these developments could eventually increase the experiment's data collection rate by another factor of ten.

Collecting much larger datasets would allow physicists to detect more of these extremely rare decays and measure their properties with greater precision. That increased sensitivity could make it possible to identify subtle effects associated with particles that remain beyond the direct reach of existing accelerators.

"Seeing evidence of this rare decay is incredibly exciting, opening up fresh possibilities to probe beyond the direct reach of the LHC," explained Harry Cliff, LHCb's Rare Decays Convener and Analysis Co-lead.

"The future LHCb upgrade will allow us to observe many more of these decays, providing even greater sensitivity to undiscovered particles.".

For physicists who have pursued this elusive signal for more than four decades, the new evidence represents a long-awaited advance. It also offers a promising way to investigate whether the known laws of particle physics are part of a much larger picture.

'Arrival' at 10: Denis Villeneuve's alien visitation classic that reminded us it's good to talk

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1716 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in many of the biggest science fiction franchises, conversing with alien races is an absolute doddle.
  • Sources indicate that but in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak.
  • The film's journey to the big screen began when a screenwriter best known for his work on horror franchises such as "Final Destination", "A Nightmare on Elm Street" and "The Thing" read a short story in an online magazine.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in many of the biggest science fiction franchises, conversing with alien races is an absolute doddle. In "Star Trek", universal translators come as standard, while C-3PO has spent the last 49 years reminding everyone in "Star Wars" that he's fluent in over six million forms of communication.

Sources indicate that but in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak. In fact, working out how to establish a dialogue with extraterrestrial visitors becomes the whole point of this powerful and heartbreaking story, as the fate of planet Earth hinges on the interpretation of a single noun.

The film's journey to the big screen began when a screenwriter best known for his work on horror franchises such as "Final Destination", "A Nightmare on Elm Street" and "The Thing" read a short story in an online magazine. Eric Heisserer was so impressed by Ted Chiang's "Understand" that he bought himself a collection of the author's short stories. One in particular, the Nebula Award-winning "Story of Your Life", piqued his interest.

"It had a very profound emotional effect on me," he reminisced to Deadline. "I was in tears, and I was both heartbroken and uplifted. My head was just full of big ideas. I had to walk around the block a couple of times afterward and just hug my friends. The next day, I was like, 'Oh god, I want to give this to other people.'".

So when 21 Laps (the production manufacturer that later went on to make "Stranger Things") invited Heisserer to discuss possible future projects, the writer mentioned "Story of Your Life". The producers were also smitten.

"I was so excited, but I had that dread that a lot of producers get, which is, 'Are the rights available?'" 21 Laps' Dan Levine told the Hollywood Gold podcast. "You read something that blows you away, and then you find there aren't the rights, and there's no chance, you have to move on. So we were trying to track down this Ted Chiang, and he had no agent. He had a day job. He was impossible to find, so we started the hunt for Ted Chiang.".

Industry observers note that an up-and-coming Canadian director named Denis Villeneuve had also found his way on to 21 Laps' radar after his 2010 French-language drama "Incendies" earned rave reviews and an Academy Award nomination. He told the producers that he'd always wanted to direct a science fiction film — a hint of things to come? — and they indicated him "Story of Your Life".

He was also drawn to the story, while the now-located Chiang was suitably impressed by the director's work on "Incendies" to make a deal for the rights. And with Amy Adams also interested in playing the lead role of linguist Dr Louise Banks, the film that would eventually become "Arrival" was ready to proceed — or, at least, it would be once Villeneuve had completed his first three Hollywood movies, "Prisoners" (2013), "Enemy" (2013) and "Sicario" (2015).

With 12 alien spaceships arriving simultaneously around the globe, "Arrival"'s poster-friendly elevator pitch could almost have been borrowed from "Independence Day". Indeed, the question of whether these whisper-quiet, chocolate button-shaped craft belong to the "Day the Earth Stood Still" / "Close Encounters" friendly extraterrestrial camp, or have the invasion of planet Earth on their minds is a mystery the world's governments are desperate to solve.

"Denis didn't really see this as an alien invasion movie — more an alien arrival movie," producer Aaron Ryder told SFX magazine. "What would be the protocols that were in place? How would they be implemented? How would people react? What would the government be doing? What would the news organisations be saying? That was the tone and the texture, which is established right up front.".

These Hollywood blockbuster components were not part of "Story of Your Life". But even though Heisserer's script was not a direct translation of Chiang's tale, he retained the most important bits — namely Dr Banks' efforts to establish a means of communication with seven-legged extraterrestrial heptapods, and the profound effect their language has on her perception of time.

In a recent development, designed by Carlos Huante, the heptapods themselves are like giant elongated hands, alien visitors light years away from the "Star Trek" tradition of actors with a few ridges glued to their foreheads. Like the evil 456 in "Torchwood: Children of Earth", they're enclosed in gaseous chambers and make sounds imperceptible to the human ear.

In a recent development, this, however, is where "Arrival" gets really interesting. Working alongside physicist colleague Dr Ian Donnelly (Jeremy Renner), Banks gradually exchanges foundational vocabulary with two heptapods they name Abbott and Costello. They discover that the alien visitors use a sophisticated written language of circular "logograms", squirted into their atmosphere as if it were sentient squid ink.

"The idea in the short story is of circular language that has no beginning and no end," Villeneuve explained in an interview with IndieWire. "We were looking for no relation to any human language. I had to figure out how to produce logograms from my aliens while avoiding being long and boring. The sounds were an expression of their emotions, with more intellect coming from the signs. This beautiful species uses written language as their first means of expression instead of movement or gesture. They produce words out of their bodies.".

According to recent reports, but Banks and Donnelly's research project has a purpose. With the world's military on high alert — and, ironically, struggling to communicate — they need to work out how to ask the aliens a fundamental question: Why are you here?

The heptapods' answer — "offer weapon" — is tantalizingly ambiguous. Are they planning to attack? Or is, as Banks suggests, 'weapon' simply being used as a synonym for 'tool'?

Aside from a bomb planted on the heptapod ship by a rogue US soldier, "Arrival" is mostly free from the significant-budget explosions that are part-and-parcel of most alien visitation movies. Instead, the film's denouement delivers a twist — the crux of Chiang's story — that rivals "The Sixth Sense", "Fight Club" and "The Prestige" in its audacious sleight of hand.

It turns out the "weapon" in question is actually the heptapod language, which, thanks to their non-linear perception of time, gives speakers a unique perspective on the past, present, and future. Therefore, those scenes we assumed to be flashbacks to the life and tragic death of Louise's daughter, Hannah, are actually flashforwards, as her increased understanding of heptapod-speak gives her memories of a life she hasn't yet lived.

Villeneuve put on multiple test screenings to ensure the big reveals hit properly.

Industry observers note that "I wanted to screen it with people who knew nothing about the project," he remarked. "What we discovered is when someone in the audience felt too lost — if intellectually they were not engaged — the ending was less powerful from an emotional point of view. So we tried to give as few clues as possible, but enough clues to be able to stay engaged and follow the story.".

Those subtle hints become obvious on second and third viewings, whether it's a lingering shot of a wedding ring absent in the movie's "present" or a conversation about the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis (the notion that the structure of a language can influence the way its speakers think). The absence of young Hannah's father also takes on tragic new meaning when we realize it's Ian, who'll leave after Louise tells him about their daughter's sad fate.

Sources indicate that "We were walking on this tightrope of trying to play things so it could play both ways, because of the reveal at the end," Adams recalled in a Vanity Fair conversation with Villeneuve. "I had to do so much work to understand how I play a character so that the first time you watch it you think that it's one thing, and the second time you watch it you can see it from a totally different perspective.".

According to recent reports, while Adams didn't get the Oscar nomination her performance deserved, everything else paid off, with the film making over $200 million worldwide from its reported $47 million budget. (The film did win an Academy Award for sound editing, while receiving further nods for best picture, director, and adapted screenplay.).

Villeneuve has famously gone on to become Hollywood's go-to guy for intelligent sci-fi, thanks to "Blade Runner 2049" and the smash-hit "Dune" saga, and will next be given the opportunity to resurrect James Bond.

Normally we'd take this opportunity to say no one could have foreseen Villeneuve's subsequent ascendancy but — in a story involving heptapods and some clever people at 21 Laps — who can be so sure?

"Arrival" is available to stream on Paramount+ in the US, and Netflix in the UK.. It's also available on Blu-ray via Amazon.

When mysterious spacecraft touch down across the globe, an elite team — led by expert codebreaker Louise Banks (Amy Adams) — is brought together to investigate.

Sources indicate that richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor.

Industry observers note that he's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.

How measuring the state of nature can reverse biodiversity loss

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1902 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the world’s largest wildlife bridge is under construction in Agoura Hills, California, and will enable animals to cross US Route 101 safely.
  • Biodiversity is the cornerstone of human survival — providing us with food, shelter, medicines, clean air and water, and contributing to our general well-being.
  • To build a better world, stop chasing economic growth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the world’s largest wildlife bridge is under construction in Agoura Hills, California, and will enable animals to cross US Route 101 safely. Credit: Kevin Carter/Getty.

Biodiversity is the cornerstone of human survival — providing us with food, shelter, medicines, clean air and water, and contributing to our general well-being. Its continuing loss is a major risk to us and to the global economy.

To build a better world, stop chasing economic growth.

To build a better world, stop chasing economic growth.

Industry observers note that extreme degradation of ecosystems is projected to cost the world at least US$2.7 trillion, or 2.3% of global gross domestic product, each year by 20301. That’s almost three times more than the annual cost of protecting nature (up to $967 billion)2, a figure that happens to be similar to the amount governments paid in 2024 to subsidize the fossil-fuel industry ($920 billion; see go.nature.com/4ejtafn).

According to recent reports, those stark numbers should drive efforts to protect nature. In 2022, the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework set out an ambitious pathway to reach the vision of a world living in harmony with nature by 20503. But what’s missing is a way to measure progress. A systematic approach to tracking biodiversity losses and attempts to reverse them is urgently needed.

Industry observers note that the Nature Positive Initiative (NPI) has begun to do this by developing metrics to record the ‘state of nature’. Launched in 2023, the NPI is a consortium of the world’s largest sustainable business and finance coalitions and conservation organizations.

Cities and countryside are intimately linked — green initiatives must recognize that.

Cities and countryside are intimately linked — green initiatives must recognize that.

Industry observers note that the metrics aim to provide a globally consistent minimal framework — a simple common language — for tracking changes in nature across countries and sectors. They were developed through a consensus process and measure ecosystem extent and condition, species extinction risks and population trends across terrestrial, freshwater and marine realms4.

According to recent reports, they are also designed to integrate with existing global standards and frameworks for reporting and disclosing nature-related financial risks, such as the Science Based Targets Network (SBTN)5 and the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD)6. This compatibility increases the likelihood that scientifically sound metrics will be reported and embedded by businesses and financial institutions in their disclosures and policies, and in systems for risk management and investment — all of which are essential to decision-making.

According to recent reports, so far, the metrics have been tested with 29 companies across 23 countries at more than 50 sites. However, they still need rigorous, independent assessment in real-world contexts to ascertain whether they are practical to implement and really improve environmental outcomes. Without empirical validation, there is a risk that these nature metrics might generate misleading signals to investors, fail to detect meaningful ecological change or impose monitoring cost burdens that limit the uptake of biodiversity projects.

Here we highlight four challenges and a way forward.

It has been revealed that although they are called metrics, the NPI measures are in fact a broad framework of indicators and recording approaches. Their focus on assessing the broad ‘state’ of ecosystems, rather than concentrating on the pressures on nature or actions for protection, is an important shift. It moves companies away from simply reporting their activities, instead making them and others accountable for outcomes. But it leaves latitude in how organizations will interpret and apply the metrics, potentially weakening their overall impact.

Sources indicate that for example, the metrics have three levels of detail or precision — preparatory, medium and high — to recognize the uneven global distribution of data, expertise and resources. Although this flexibility makes them easier to apply in diverse settings, it creates challenges for comparability and interpretation when assessments are undertaken on different spatial scales or levels of precision.

The Tiaozini wetlands in eastern China are a crucial ecological hub.Credit: Costfoto/NurPhoto via Getty.

In a recent development, the idea is that companies will get on board early with the preparatory level of precision and then progress towards more high-quality, ecologically meaningful measures and outcomes. A preparatory-level assessment might use data with relatively coarse spatial resolution and classify land cover as natural or not natural, for instance. More-advanced assessments would have higher resolution and use more-precise ecosystem classifications.

The concern is that organizations might cherry-pick ‘easy’ ecosystem characteristics or species to measure, potentially biasing their reporting towards apparent gains rather than describing those that are meaningful. For instance, common species are more likely to respond well to ecological improvements than specialist species are, even though the specialists might be a higher priority for conservation.

Over-reporting of improvements, particularly in relation to ecosystem connectivity and extent, can provide a misleading sense of how well species can survive genetic and demographic challenges. Better understanding of these measures is also important in guarding against changes that might not only bring benefits but also could do harm, such as when connectivity promotes the movement of invasive species that alter the local ecosystem.

Another challenge is that nature is forever changing through a myriad of interactions between living species and the environment, as well as with shifting global processes such as climate change. With simple metrics, there is a risk that complex, dynamic processes and non-linear changes will be missed and the damages and risks underestimated.

How biodiversity credits could help to conserve and restore nature.

How biodiversity credits could help to conserve and restore nature.

Measuring the number of hectares restored, for instance, can indicate where conservation action has occurred, but not whether nature has recovered, ecosystem functions have been reinstated or threatened species populations are increasing.

The inclusion of ecosystem condition and species status measures in the NPI metrics aim to address this complexity. But this will work only if they are not simplified to the point at which they no longer provide an accurate and comprehensive assessment of how a site is changing.

Reconciling the tension between a global approach for nature impacts and the local ecological and sociopolitical experiences of these impacts is challenging. Although global consistency is essential for corporate reporting so that investors can make informed comparisons, at the local level, biodiversity protection and the financial impacts and dependencies of communities on natural resources are inherently context-specific. Metrics designed to support global comparisons between organizations might overlook ecological, cultural and social values that are crucial locally.

Why environmental treaties must also address mental health.

Why environmental treaties must also address mental health.

Many users of the state of nature metrics and global biodiversity frameworks will draw heavily on global data sets. Such resources include the Global Forest Watch Open Data Portal and the Copernicus Global Dynamic Land Cover product for ecosystem extent and condition, and the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species as a proxy for species that are at risk of extinction.

But without on-the-ground verification, the metrics will fail, particularly in data-poor regions, by misrepresenting fine-scale ecological conditions and changes. Relying on remote-sensing products that describe only the tree canopy, for example, can miss much about the structure of the forest below. Indigenous knowledges might also be disregarded. Overlooking local values and knowledge is concerning because it reinforces the broader global pattern of marginalizing local communities in environmental decision-making.

Implementation of the metrics and the incentives behind them that push companies to engage with nature measurement are likely to have both positive and negative impacts on nature and communities. What these impacts look like is currently unknown. This is why the metrics need to be independently tested to assess their value for nature, businesses and communities.

Impacts on nature will be driven by how priority species are determined, how the metrics are combined and compared and the time frame in which changes will be measured. For example, should equal weight be given to population change in critically endangered species and to species of important cultural value to local communities?

Recent findings suggest that and how should customers compare shifts in the components of an ecosystem that typically change over decades (such as growth of a forest) to those that develop much more rapidly (such as the life cycles of pollinating insects)? Developing guidance on how to grapple with these complexities will be essential if the metrics are to describe the state of nature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Head coach excited by ‘high potential’ of players.

Striker Goodwin and keeper Cox in squad for first time.

Sarina Wiegman indicates the potential in England’s emerging young players helped convince her to extend her contract until the end of 2029’s European Championship.

The Lionesses head coach, whose previous deal was due to expire next year, gave first senior call-ups to the striker Isobel Goodwin and goalkeeper Katie Cox on Tuesday as she named her squad for December’s two-leg World Cup qualifying playoff against Ukraine.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to the media for the first time since signed her upcoming contract in October, Wiegman described the Football Association as “a trailblazer with the women’s game and a great federation to work for” and mentioned: “I’m really happy with the team but also talents coming through, which is exciting, and there’s now some high potential, and hopefully these talents go from high potential to world-class players, if not already. And I hope to have a part in that, too, and have a contribution to that. While I’m talking about that, I’m getting excited.

“The majority of their development is happening [at their clubs] but when they come to our environment, I hope to have a little part of that contribution.”.

The Dutchwoman has led England to three consecutive major tournament finals, lifting two European titles, since taking charge in 2021 on a deal to 2025. Asked whether she had expected that to become an eight-year stay, she noted: “No. I thought: ‘Four years, that’s a long time.’ Then it became six years and that looks like it’s becoming eight years. I would never have expected all of the things that we have reached.”.

According to recent reports, will she call it a day in 2029? “Well, I tend to think that’s the end point, but you never know! I don’t proposal that far ahead. So let’s see where it gets to.”.

Goalkeepers: Katie Cox (Nottingham Forest on loan from Chelsea), Hannah Hampton (Chelsea), Khiara Keating (Liverpool)Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea), Jess Carter (Gotham), Grace Fisk (Liverpool), Taylor Hinds (Arsenal), Maya Le Tissier (Manchester United), Esme Morgan (Washington Spirit), Poppy Pattinson (London City Lionesses), Leah Williamson (Arsenal)Midfielders: Laura Blindkilde Brown (Manchester City), Grace Clinton (Manchester City), Erica Meg Parkinson (North Carolina Courage), Lexi Potter (Chelsea), Georgia Stanway (Arsenal), Ella Toone (Manchester United), Keira Walsh (Chelsea)Forwards: Aggie Beever-Jones (Chelsea), Freya Godfrey (London City Lionesses), Isobel Goodwin (London City Lionesses), Lauren Hemp (Manchester City), Beth Mead (Manchester City), Jess Park (Manchester United), Alessia Russo (Arsenal).

Recent findings suggest that wiegman, whose latest 25-player squad includes 10 players with fewer than 10 caps, watched from the stands at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday as Goodwin scored for London City Lionesses with a terrific finish against Arsenal. She noted of the 23-year-old: “We always knew she’s a huge talent [with] a high potential. We’re watching a lot of games over periods of time, all the time, so we [had] kept an eye on her anyway, but I think it also helped that she had that great goal and a great performance last Sunday.

“She has some different qualities. She’s really fast too. She can head – she demonstrated that also in attacking set plays and defending set plays also – and she can score goals. Does she need to step up to the next level? Absolutely. But you can tell that she’s improving.”.

Wiegman was unable to call upon several injured players, including Lauren James and Alex Greenwood. She included Manchester United’s Ella Toone, who was initially left out of September’s squad before being recalled for the playoff against Greece. Wiegman said of Toone: “She has impressed us really well. She responded really well. And going back to [her] club, she’s done well too. And that’s what has been fed back to me too.”.

It has been revealed that cox is rare in getting an England call-up while playing in the second-tier WSL2. The 20-year-old is on loan at Nottingham Forest from Chelsea.

The Lionesses face Ukraine on neutral territory in Spain in the away leg on 1 December before playing them at Wembley four days later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Izzy Goodwin has scored three goals in five WSL appearances for London City.

London City Lionesses forward Izzy Goodwin has been named in the England squad for the first time for the World Cup qualifying play-off against Ukraine.

The 23-year-old has been in great form this month and scored in front of England manager Sarina Wiegman at Emirates Stadium on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Arsenal.

"We have always seen her as a huge talent with potential," Wiegman told BBC Radio 5 Live.

#13000. Breaking: NASA reveals bold new proposal to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028

Breaking: NASA reveals bold new proposal to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1370 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that NASA has revealed newly introduced details about its accelerated effort to return American astronauts to the Moon in 2028.
  • According to recent reports, during an October 23 briefing, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and other agency leaders outlined the next steps for the Artemis program.
  • Sources indicate that the announcement builds on priorities introduced earlier this year through NASA's Ignition initiative.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that NASA has revealed newly introduced details about its accelerated effort to return American astronauts to the Moon in 2028. The updated strategy includes testing two competing lunar landers, streamlining rocket preparations, and introducing a lighter spacesuit to help make the first moonwalks possible sooner.

According to recent reports, during an October 23 briefing, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and other agency leaders outlined the next steps for the Artemis program. The revised approach centers on two major missions: Artemis III, a test flight scheduled for 2027, and Artemis IV, which is intended to land astronauts on the lunar surface in 2028.

Sources indicate that the announcement builds on priorities introduced earlier this year through NASA's Ignition initiative. Agency officials also highlighted recent progress in spacecraft development, mission preparations, and partnerships with private aerospace companies. These efforts are intended to reduce technical risks, accelerate the schedule, and establish the foundation for a lasting American presence on the Moon.

"This is a very energized NASA, and these updates are only a small part of that story. We are bringing extreme focus to the mission to ensure delivery of world-changing outcomes as promptly, safely, affordably, and successfully as possible," said Isaacman. "NASA is driving outcomes to make Moon missions a reality, and we're not waiting for others to bring their aims to us -- the campaign must move with urgency as strategic competitors pursue a permanent presence beyond Earth.".

Artemis III Will Test Two Lunar Landers in Earth Orbit.

Before attempting another crewed Moon landing, NASA plans to conduct a major rehearsal in Earth orbit. The Artemis III mission will bring together NASA's Orion spacecraft and experimental lunar landers developed by SpaceX and Blue Origin.

Four astronauts will travel aboard Orion, launching on NASA's powerful SLS (Space Launch System) rocket. During the planned 14-day mission, the crew will practice rendezvous and docking procedures with both companies' lander test vehicles. Rendezvous involves guiding two spacecraft to meet in orbit, while docking allows them to connect so astronauts can move between vehicles.

These demonstrations are designed to verify crucial spacecraft capabilities before Artemis IV attempts to carry astronauts to the Moon's surface.

The tests will take place in a carefully planned sequence. Blue Origin will first launch a test version of its Blue Moon lander into Earth orbit. NASA will then send Orion and its four astronauts into space aboard the SLS rocket, where Orion will rendezvous and dock with the Blue Moon vehicle.

According to recent reports, next, SpaceX will launch a test version of its Version 3 Starship lunar lander. Orion will separate from Blue Moon and perform another docking maneuver, this time with Starship. By testing both systems during a single crewed mission, NASA aims to gather essential operational experience while reducing uncertainties before the 2028 landing attempt.

NASA Cuts Rocket Preparation Times and Costs.

The new mission details follow other recent Artemis progress reports. According to NASA, the hardware needed for Artemis III remains on schedule, and improvements in processing have reduced preparation timelines by approximately 50%.

The agency also reported a significant engineering achievement involving a critical rocket fuel-line component. Rather than relying on an outside supplier, NASA engineers redesigned, manufactured, and tested the component themselves in just five months. The work cost roughly one-tenth of an earlier estimate from an external vendor.

Sources indicate that "NASA should be expected to do this kind of work, and we have some of the best technical knowledge in the world on rocket hardware and operations to do it," mentioned Jeremy Parsons, the agency's Artemis program manager. "It's an example of how we are rebuilding our core competencies and developing centers of excellence in technical functions instead of continuing to outsource expertise.".

The improvements reflect NASA's broader effort to strengthen its internal engineering capabilities, shorten development schedules, and reduce the cost of preparing missions for launch.

SpaceX and Blue Origin Offer Different Paths to the Moon.

For Artemis IV in 2028, NASA intends to launch astronauts aboard Orion using the SLS rocket from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Once in space, the crew will rely on a lunar landing system developed by either SpaceX or Blue Origin to reach the Moon's surface.

Both companies have revised their original mission designs to make operations simpler, more efficient, and more adaptable. Although they share the same objective, their approaches to transporting astronauts to the lunar surface differ considerably.

Sources indicate that spaceX plans to use its Starship spacecraft, which will take on additional propellant while orbiting Earth. After refueling, Starship will meet Orion and carry the spacecraft toward the Moon. Refueling in orbit is an key part of SpaceX's strategy because it allows the vehicle to receive the propellant needed for its journey after leaving the launchpad.

Recent findings suggest that blue Origin is developing a different approach using its Blue Moon Mark 2 lander. Its plan calls for additional propulsion stages in Earth orbit to send the lander toward the Moon. The lander will then meet Orion in a relatively low lunar orbit before carrying astronauts down to the surface.

According to recent reports, both companies are working toward having their systems ready to support a crewed Moon landing in 2028. Maintaining two potential landing systems gives NASA greater flexibility as development and testing continue.

NASA Explores New Rocket Options for Artemis IV.

Recent findings suggest that NASA is also considering two possible upper stages for the SLS rocket used on Artemis IV. An upper stage is the portion of a rocket that provides additional propulsion after the earlier stages have completed their work, helping send a spacecraft toward its destination.

It has been revealed that one option is the interim cryogenic propulsion stage already used by SLS. The other is an extended version of United Launch Alliance's Centaur V upper stage, which would hold additional propellant.

Recent findings suggest that by developing both possibilities, NASA hopes to preserve flexibility in its launch plans and avoid becoming dependent on a single technical solution. Having alternatives could help the agency respond to engineering challenges without jeopardizing the broader Moon landing schedule.

A New Lightweight Spacesuit Could Speed Up Moonwalks.

Another important change involves the spacesuits astronauts will wear while exploring the lunar surface.

NASA is working with Axiom Space on a second, lighter design known as the "Sortie suit." The new suit is intended specifically for the first Moon surface excursions and weighs approximately half as much as Axiom's larger primary spacesuit.

The lighter design could simplify preparations for the earliest landing missions and help astronauts begin exploring the lunar surface sooner.

However, the Sortie suit is not intended to replace the primary design. Axiom's more capable suit will remain part of NASA's prepares for future missions that require longer periods outside the spacecraft and more demanding surface activities.

Building a Permanent Human Presence on the Moon.

NASA's ambitions extend well beyond returning astronauts to the lunar surface for a single mission.

As the Artemis program advances, the agency intends to send crews on increasingly challenging expeditions near the Moon's South Pole. This region is an key focus of future lunar exploration, and the missions are designed to expand how much of the Moon humans can investigate directly.

According to recent reports, NASA describes the effort as part of a new Golden Age of innovation and exploration. The agency expects its lunar missions to support scientific discoveries, generate economic benefits, and encourage the development of technologies needed for more ambitious space exploration.

Ultimately, the goal is to establish an enduring human presence on the Moon rather than repeat the brief visits of earlier lunar expeditions. The experience gained from operating spacecraft, supporting astronauts, and carrying out increasingly complex missions on the lunar surface will also help NASA prepare for another historic objective: sending the first astronauts to Mars.

Sports journalist Jose de Jesus Ortiz called Reese’s actions “classless,” while former ESPN host Keith Olbermann called Reese an “idiot” for the gesture.

In the press conference after the victory, Reese referenced the difference in reaction she received as a result of her gesture as compared to the one Clark received.

According to recent reports, “All year, I was critiqued for who I was. I don’t fit the narrative,” Reese remarked. “I don’t fit the box that y’all want me to be in. I’m too hood. I’m too ghetto. Y’all told me that all year. But when other people do it, and y’all don’t say nothing.

Sources indicate that “And I’m happy. I feel like I’ve helped grow women’s basketball this year. (…) I’m looking forward to celebrating and then next season.”.

LSU beats Iowa to win its first NCAA women's basketball championship.

Reese had 15 points and 10 rebounds in the 102-85 victory and won the women’s March Madness’ Most Outstanding Player award.

In the post-game broadcast, Reese referenced the similar gesture Clark made to a Louisville opponent in the Elite Eight.

In the same game, Clark mentioned to an opponent: “You’re down by 15 points. Shut up,” according to the Bleacher Report.

“Caitlin Clark is a hell of a player but I don’t take disrespect lightly,” Reese said. “She disrespected [LSU’s] Alexis [Morris] (…) and I wanted to pick her pocket. But I had a moment at the end of her game. I was in my bag, I was in my moment.”.

After the Championship game, Clark herself stated she didn’t notice anything at the time.

It has been revealed that “I was just trying to get to the handshake line and shake hands and be grateful that my team was in that position,” Clark said in the post-game press conference. “All the credit in the world to LSU. They were tremendous. They deserve it. They had a tremendous season.

“(LSU head coach) Kim Mulkey coached them so, so well. She’s one of the best basketball coaches of all time, and it demonstrates. She only stated really kind things to me in the handshake line, so I’m very grateful of that too.

“But honestly I have no idea. I was just trying to spend the last few moments on the court with especially the five people that I’ve started 93 games with and relishing every second of that.”.

LSU head coach Mulkey said she had “no clue” about what transpired.

Among those defending Reese on social media were ESPN’s Holly Rowe and former NBA star Etan Thomas.

Recent findings suggest that “People hating on Angel Reese or Caitlin Clark. Stop. Unapologetically confident young women should be celebrated NOT hated. Get used to it,” Rowe wrote on Twitter.

Former Washington Wizards, Oklahoma City Thunder and Atlanta Hawks player Thomas wrote: “Hold on now!!!! It was cute when Caitlin Clark did it. Y’all didn’t have any issues with it at all. So don’t be all outraged and talking about class and sportsmanship when Angel Reese does the same thing. We’re not doing double standards here.”.

Reese remarked the negative reaction on social media throughout the season has helped fuel her excellent season, having finished averaging 23.0 points and 15.4 rebounds in her first season with LSU after transferring from Maryland.

“Twitter can say what they want to say,” she stated. “I love reading those comments. I have all the screenshots of what everybody has said about me all season. What are you going to say now?”.

How to Run SteamOS on Your Mac

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (824 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most of my Steam collection won't run on my Mac.
  • I will be the first to admit that my collection is mostly old indie games, all of which work fine on Windows.
  • Industry observers note that but there's another way.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most of my Steam collection won't run on my Mac. It's not (entirely) my fault.

I will be the first to admit that my collection is mostly old indie games, all of which work fine on Windows. Less so on the Mac. Apple stopped supporting 32-bit games back in 2019 when it released macOS Catalina. A good chunk of my Steam library has a "No" symbol next to it because of that restriction. And next year it will get even worse: macOS will drop support for running Intel Mac applications, which could leave even more games unplayable (though Apple claims that certain older games will keep working).

Industry observers note that but there's another way. A free, open source app called FX Steam Launcher boots the ARM version of SteamOS—the operating system that powers Valve's Steam Deck gaming handheld—right on your Mac, using a combination of a virtual machine and compatibility layers. You will need a Mac with an Apple Silicon processor, as Intel Macs aren't supported, running macOS 15 or later. I set this up recently, connected a controller, and I've been playing all kinds of games that are otherwise unplayable on my MacBook Air.

Industry observers note that it wasn't even hard to set up. To get started, download the application, mount the DMG file, and drag the app to your Applications folder. The first time you launch the application, a pop-up will offer to download and install SteamOS for you in a virtual machine.

In a recent development, click Create Fresh Disk, and you'll be asked a few questions. The most important step is the hard drive size—the default is 64 GB, which is plenty, but consider allocating more space if you plan on installing multiple large games. You can also choose the drive location, if you like, and set a password for opening SteamOS.

Click Create, and the application will download SteamOS and install it in a virtual machine. I recommend using this time to pair a game controller with your Mac in System Settings under Bluetooth. FX Steam Launcher works with most current gamepads, including Xbox, DualSense, DualShock, and Made for iPhone. I used a Nintendo Pro Controller.

Eventually, you will see the login screen, where you can enter your Steam credentials. Once you're in, you'll see your Steam library. The virtual machine operates like an actual Steam Deck, which takes some getting used to if you've never used one. It divides your library into games known to work in SteamOS and those that might work, which is helpful. A lot of my games started running immediately, with full gamepad support.

This isn't a drop-in solution for every game. SteamOS itself is quite fiddly, and you're now running it in a virtual machine. In some cases, I needed to tweak the graphics settings for games to run correctly. For Psychonauts, specifically, I had to download a user-made patch to get the controller working properly—but I'd have needed that fix for an actual Steam Deck too. When a game ran poorly, I frequently found the solution by Googling and finding actual Steam Deck owners who ran into similar problems.

There is a limit to the processing power you get out of a Mac, especially if you (like me) are using a MacBook Air. And a virtual machine, by definition, doesn't have access to all of your machine's capabilities. But the list of compatible games, compiled from other users, shows which devices have successfully played various titles. Check that page for your favorite games before you dive in.

Recent findings suggest that if nothing else, this is a lot easier than my previous method for running Windows games on a Mac, which involved setting up a version of Wine that's no longer supported. I even got a few non-Steam games installed. Sideloading on SteamOS means booting into Desktop Mode, which you can find in the SteamOS sidebar under Power. You'll end up in a Linux-based desktop, complete with a web browser. You can download games, put them in the folder of your choice, and point Steam to them. I couldn't add custom art, but I got multiple games up and running this way.

Honestly, Valve should revision the official Steam Mac client with similar compatibility tech so it can run Windows games natively. It would be a huge hit with Mac users.

Recent findings suggest that if you're a power user, I recommend checking out the settings for FX Steam Launcher, which you can open from the menu bar or with the keyboard shortcut Command-comma. You can change the resolution for your virtual Steam Deck, configure the sound to your liking, and submit game statistics.

It's remarkable software. And, with an HDMI cable and a gamepad, you can plug your MacBook into your TV and game from your couch. That's what I plan on doing when I'm done writing this article (which I guess is right now).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation.
  • “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina.
  • The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation.

“Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker remarked yes.

The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material.

It has been revealed that “There are two types of humans,” Jorge Valdano narrates, “Carlos Bilardo and everyone else.” Ricardo “El Gringo” Giusti recounts how he buried a sweet in the pitch before kick-off of every game, just one of the many cábalas the Argentina squad religiously followed under pressure from their obsessive manager. On the eve of the match with England, the players requested lighter shirts as the official ones were too heavy when drenched in sweat. Footage of women working at the squad hotel hand-stitching the numbers on to light T-shirts bought locally, shot by the players themselves with a handheld camera, conveys an intimacy in stark contrast to grainy archive material depicting British explorers in the South Atlantic.

Recent findings suggest that rather than run-of-the-mill talking head-style interviews with members of both teams, the interviewees are shot in monochrome, widescreen closeups, “like Roman statues”, as Cabral told the Guardian. Like monuments to themselves, the camera lingers on their eyes. What are they watching? We don’t know if they see what we see, if they are reliving the match, or seeing a cut of the actual film.

It has been revealed that the documentary pivots around Diego Maradona’s two goals. I have long ceased to think of them as two separate goals. They are a single event, a handful of minutes when everything that is possible in football happened before our very eyes: the ugly, rule-breaking handball followed by the spectacular, beautiful gambeta. The film cleverly uses a sequence of stills taken by the Mexican photographer Alejandro Ojeda Carbajal to prove the handball, with a tongue-in-cheek nod to the paradox that they have been credited and licensed through the Englishman Bob Thomas ever since.

Films about football are hard to get right because football is a narrative form in itself. This one comes pretty close to being as good as it gets. Slick and elegant, if at times a little too glossy, The Match is an excellent piece of work filled with beautiful images, such as the crisp vintage radio illustrating soldiers listening to the game in the trenches. There are also newsreels of Margaret Thatcher and Argentinian generals at the height of the Falklands/Malvinas conflict; a score that includes Queen and giants of Argentinian rock such as Charly García. Nostalgia, history, and the backdrop of the war, handled with respect and sensitivity.

According to recent reports, the perversity of Argentina’s military is reflected in images of an emaciated soldier spliced to the voice of a general who dismisses claims the troops were cold and starving: “They probably eat better than they did at home.” Lou Armour, a British veteran, explains he couldn’t see young Argentinians as the enemy. “We both suffered a tragedy,” Cabral says. “I’m interested in the human duality in which we go from killing each other to hugging each other.” Cabral asks when a match starts and when it ends, and also when a conflict does so.

Valdano reads Juan López y John Ward, a Jorge Luis Borges poem about the war, in Spanish. Lineker, sitting by his side, utters “very moving”, also in Spanish. English and Spanish coexist throughout the film, including in the scene showing a table football game in which John Barnes and Peter Shilton take on against Giusti, Óscar Ruggeri and Jorge Burruchaga. Burruchaga, the scorer of the winning goal in the 1986 World Cup final, cheers his opponent: “Vamos, Peter!”.

An audience containing young people reacted to the documentary with a standing ovation at the London screening, where Shilton was the only cast member present. In Buenos Aires, the release of the documentary, which coincided with this summer’s World Cup, saw cinemas packed with young people. For a generation in England and Argentina who never saw the 1986 classic, almost everything in The Match is upcoming.

The Match is in UK cinemas from 20 November.

💡 Key Takeaways
